name: MAREA
capacity: 200 Tbps — highest capacity transatlantic cable at launch
strategic_value: Primary US-Europe backbone. Bypasses UK landing points, landing directly in Bilbao, Spain. Reduces single-point-of-failure risk at Cornwall.
tag: HIGHEST-CAPACITY TRANSATLANTIC CABLE

name: Dunant
strategic_value: Google-owned private transatlantic cable. Virginia Beach to Saint-Hilaire-de-Riez, France. Gives Google sovereign control over US-Europe data routing.
tag: GOOGLE PRIVATE TRANSATLANTIC

name: Grace Hopper
strategic_value: Three-way landing: New York to Bude (UK) and Bilbao (Spain). Named after computing pioneer. Strengthens Google's private network backbone across NATO allies.
tag: GOOGLE THREE-WAY TRANSATLANTIC

name: AEConnect-1
strategic_value: US to Ireland direct cable. Connects to major data center hub in Dublin. Critical for US tech companies' European operations.
tag: US-IRELAND DIRECT LINK

name: SEA-ME-WE 6
builder: SubCom (US) — deliberately excluded Huawei Marine from contract
strategic_value: Designed as Western-aligned alternative to SEA-ME-WE 5. SubCom won contract after US lobbied against Huawei Marine. Routes through Singapore, India, Djibouti, Egypt, Europe.
tag: WESTERN COUNTER TO HUAWEI CABLE DOMINANCE
alert: Transits Red Sea cable corridor — vulnerable to Houthi disruption

name: 2Africa
capacity: 180 Tbps — largest subsea cable project ever at announcement
strategic_value: Circumnavigates entire African continent with extensions to Middle East. 45,000 km. Connects 33 countries. Meta's bid to control Africa's internet backbone and bypass Chinese-built cables.
tag: LARGEST SUBMARINE CABLE PROJECT — META'S AFRICA RING
alert: Red Sea segment at risk; multiple East African landing stations near Chinese-operated ports

name: Equiano
strategic_value: Google-owned cable from Portugal to South Africa along West African coast. 20x more capacity than previous cables serving the region. Named after Olaudah Equiano.
tag: GOOGLE'S WEST AFRICA BACKBONE

name: PEACE Cable (Pakistan & East Africa Connecting Europe)
strategic_value: China's flagship submarine cable project. Pakistan to France via East Africa and Egypt. Connects Gwadar (CPEC terminus) directly to Europe. Lands at Marseille — Europe's largest interconnection hub.
tag: CHINA'S DIGITAL SILK ROAD BACKBONE — BRI UNDERSEA
alert: Western intelligence agencies flag data interception risk at Chinese-controlled landing stations

name: SEA-ME-WE 5
strategic_value: Huawei Marine's landmark build — proved Chinese firms could deliver major intercontinental cable systems. Triggered US campaign to block Huawei from future contracts (SEA-ME-WE 6 awarded to SubCom).
tag: HUAWEI MARINE FLAGSHIP — TRIGGERED US CABLE WAR
alert: US intelligence concerns over Huawei-built repeaters and potential backdoor access

name: Asia-Africa-Europe-1 (AAE-1)
owner: Consortium (19 telcos including China Unicom, VNPT)
strategic_value: Mixed consortium cable connecting East Asia to Europe via Southeast Asia, India, Middle East, Africa. Chinese telcos hold significant stake. Routes through every major chokepoint.
tag: ASIA-EUROPE ARTERY — MIXED OWNERSHIP
alert: Transits Red Sea, Suez, Strait of Malacca — triple chokepoint exposure

name: SAIL (South Atlantic Inter Link)
strategic_value: First direct China-backed cable connecting Africa to South America. Cameroon to Fortaleza, Brazil. Bypasses all Western-controlled Atlantic cable infrastructure. Part of Digital Silk Road southern expansion.
tag: CHINA'S SOUTH ATLANTIC BYPASS — DIGITAL SILK ROAD
alert: Enables China to route Africa-Latin America traffic without transiting US/European cable systems

name: EASSy (East African Submarine Cable System)
strategic_value: Backbone of East African internet. Runs from South Africa to Sudan along entire East African coast. Landing stations increasingly near Chinese-operated ports (Djibouti, Mombasa, Dar es Salaam).
tag: EAST AFRICA BACKBONE — PROXIMITY TO CHINESE PORTS
alert: Chinese port operators at Djibouti and other landing cities raise intelligence concerns

name: Red Sea Cable Corridor
capacity: 14+ submarine cables transit this corridor carrying majority of Europe-Asia data traffic
strategic_value: World's most critical submarine cable chokepoint. 14+ cables pass through Bab al-Mandab strait in narrow corridor. Single anchor drag or sabotage event can sever multiple cables simultaneously.
tag: MOST VULNERABLE CABLE CHOKEPOINT ON EARTH
alert: Houthi-linked anchor-dragging incidents severed 3 cables in Feb 2024 (AAE-1, Seacom, EIG). Repairs delayed months due to Yemen conflict zone restrictions.

name: Strait of Malacca Cable Crossing
capacity: 25+ cables cross or terminate near the strait
strategic_value: Chokepoint for cables connecting East Asia to Indian Ocean and onward to Europe/Middle East. Singapore is the region's primary cable hub. Anchor damage from heavy shipping traffic is recurring threat.
tag: ASIA-EUROPE DIGITAL CHOKEPOINT
alert: Frequent anchor damage incidents due to extreme shipping density. Chinese naval expansion raises wartime severance concerns.

name: Egypt — Suez Canal Cable Corridor
owner: Telecom Egypt (state monopoly on cable landings)
capacity: 16+ cables land in Egypt — single overland transit point for Europe-Asia cables
strategic_value: Nearly ALL submarine cables from Asia to Europe must land in Egypt to cross the Suez isthmus overland. Telecom Egypt controls every landing station. Single-point-of-failure for global internet if Egypt is destabilized.
tag: SINGLE POINT OF FAILURE — EUROPE-ASIA DATA
alert: Egyptian political instability or conflict could sever majority of Europe-Asia internet traffic. No viable alternative route exists at scale.

name: Luzon Strait — Taiwan Cable Vulnerability
capacity: 14+ cables serving Taiwan, many routed through Luzon Strait
strategic_value: Taiwan's internet connectivity depends on cables running through Luzon Strait between Taiwan and Philippines. Chinese military could sever these cables as first move in Taiwan contingency, isolating the island digitally.
tag: TAIWAN DIGITAL LIFELINE — CHINA SEVERANCE THREAT
alert: PLA Navy exercises have occurred directly over cable routes. Cable cuts here would isolate Taiwan's semiconductor industry from global networks.

name: Cornwall UK — Atlantic Cable Landing Hub
capacity: Major landing point for transatlantic and Europe-global cables
strategic_value: Bude, Cornwall is the primary UK landing point for transatlantic cables and a hub for onward connections to Europe. GCHQ Bude facility co-located — Tempora program taps cables here. Single geographic concentration risk.
tag: NATO ATLANTIC CABLE HUB — GCHQ CO-LOCATED
alert: Russian submarine activity near cable routes has increased since 2014. Concentration of cables at single landing point creates vulnerability.

name: Baltic Sea Cable Cuts (2023-2024)
owner: Various (Balticconnector gas pipe + C-Lion1 cable + others)
capacity: Multiple cables and pipelines severed in suspected sabotage incidents
strategic_value: Suspected sabotage of Balticconnector pipeline (Oct 2023) and C-Lion1 Finland-Germany cable (Nov 2024), plus EstLink power cable. Chinese vessel Yi Peng 3 and Hong Kong-flagged NewNew Polar Bear investigated. Demonstrates vulnerability of undersea infrastructure to gray-zone attacks.
tag: GRAY ZONE SABOTAGE — UNDERSEA INFRASTRUCTURE ATTACKS
alert: Chinese-flagged vessels implicated in anchor-dragging incidents. NATO launched Baltic Sentry mission in response. Establishes precedent for cable warfare.

name: Taiwan Cable Severance Scenario
capacity: Taiwan served by ~14 submarine cables — all vulnerable to coordinated severance
strategic_value: Pentagon and Taiwan defense planners assess that PLA could sever all of Taiwan's submarine cables within hours as precursor to invasion or coercion campaign. Would isolate TSMC and Taiwan's tech sector from global networks. Matsu Islands cables were cut by Chinese vessels in Feb 2023 — widely seen as rehearsal.
tag: DIGITAL BLOCKADE SCENARIO — TAIWAN ISOLATION
alert: Matsu Islands cable cuts (Feb 2023) by Chinese fishing/cargo vessels demonstrated the tactic. Full Taiwan severance would be catastrophic for global semiconductor supply chain communications.

name: Djibouti Cable Landing Station
capacity: 7+ major cables land here — AAE-1, EASSy, DARE1, PEACE, SEA-ME-WE 3/5, others
strategic_value: Tiny nation hosts both largest US military base in Africa (Camp Lemonnier) AND China's first overseas military base (PLA Support Base). Both powers' intelligence agencies monitor cables landing here. Critical node where PEACE cable and Western cables physically converge.
tag: US-CHINA CABLE INTELLIGENCE BATTLEGROUND
alert: Chinese PLA base is <10km from cable landing stations. Djibouti government increasingly Beijing-aligned. US intelligence community flags data interception risk.

name: Marseille Cable Landing Hub
capacity: 13+ submarine cables — Europe's largest interconnection hub
strategic_value: Europe's primary cable landing point for traffic from Asia, Middle East, and Africa. Both Western cables and PEACE cable (Chinese) terminate here. Whoever controls Marseille's data centers controls Europe's inbound data flow.
tag: EUROPE'S DIGITAL FRONT DOOR — CONTESTED
alert: PEACE cable landing gives Chinese-backed infrastructure direct access to European interconnection hub. French intelligence (DGSE) monitors but cannot prevent data routing through Chinese-built cable segments.

name: Singapore Cable Hub
strategic_value: World's second-largest cable landing hub after New York metro area. Gateway between Indian Ocean and Pacific cable systems. Singapore maintains Western alignment while hosting Chinese cable connections. Critical IMEC digital corridor node.
tag: ASIA'S CABLE CROSSROADS — IMEC DIGITAL NODE
alert: Proximity to Strait of Malacca creates physical vulnerability. Chinese cable investments in region growing.

name: Mumbai Cable Landing Hub
strategic_value: India's digital gateway to the world. Landing point for cables to Europe (via Red Sea), Middle East, East Africa, and Southeast Asia. Key node on both IMEC and INSTC digital corridors. India playing both Western and non-aligned cable strategies.
tag: INDIA'S DIGITAL GATEWAY — IMEC/INSTC NODE
alert: Cable concentration at single metro area creates vulnerability. India increasingly building redundancy via Chennai.
